sections.title: Three Core Storage Models
paragraphs: Object, block, and file storage represent different ways to organize and access data. Selecting the model comes before selecting the service.

table.caption: Identify the storage model
rows: Raw addressable volumes used like disks
Shared files and directories through file-system protocols

sections.title: Object Storage and Amazon S3
paragraphs: Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) provides highly scalable object storage. Objects live in buckets and can include files, images, videos, backups, logs, static content, and large datasets.

sections.title: Amazon S3 Storage Classes
paragraphs: S3 storage classes provide different combinations of storage price, access cost, retrieval behavior, and resilience. Match the class to access frequency and retrieval needs.

entries.title: Frequently Accessed Data
paragraphs: Use a class designed for regular, immediate access when data is used often.

entries.title: Infrequently Accessed Data
paragraphs: Use an infrequent-access class when data must remain available but is read less often.

entries.title: Archive Data
paragraphs: Use archival classes for long-term retention when data is rarely retrieved and retrieval timing permits.

entries.title: S3 Intelligent-Tiering
paragraphs: Use when access patterns are unknown or changing; objects can move among access tiers based on usage.

sections.title: Block Storage and Amazon EBS
paragraphs: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) provides persistent block volumes designed for use with Amazon EC2. It behaves like a disk volume for operating systems, applications, and databases.
sections.callout: Persistent EC2 block volume → Amazon EBS

sections.title: Instance Store
paragraphs: Instance store provides temporary block storage physically associated with the host used by an EC2 instance. Its data does not survive certain instance lifecycle events.
sections.callout: Temporary or ephemeral local EC2 storage → Instance store

sections.title: EBS vs. Instance Store
sections.callout: EBS = KEEP IT · INSTANCE STORE = TEMPORARY

sections.title: File Storage
paragraphs: File services organize data into files and directories and provide shared file-system access through supported protocols.

entries.title: Amazon EFS
paragraphs: Amazon Elastic File System provides managed elastic shared file storage for Linux workloads using NFS.

entries.title: Amazon FSx
paragraphs: Amazon FSx provides managed file systems for specialized technologies and workloads, including Windows-oriented use cases.

sections.title: AWS Storage Gateway
paragraphs: AWS Storage Gateway connects on-premises environments with AWS cloud storage. It supports hybrid storage workflows and can maintain cached access to cloud-backed data.
sections.callout: On premises plus AWS storage or cached cloud-backed access → AWS Storage Gateway

sections.title: Lifecycle Policies
paragraphs: A lifecycle policy automates object transitions to suitable storage classes or expiration when data reaches defined ages or conditions.
sections.callout: Move or expire data automatically as it ages → Lifecycle policy

sections.title: AWS Backup
paragraphs: AWS Backup centralizes and automates backup policies, schedules, retention, and monitoring across supported AWS resources.

sections.title: GSA Scenario Recognition
bullets: Unknown changing access pattern → S3 Intelligent-Tiering
Temporary local EC2 storage → Instance store
Connect local storage workflows to AWS → Storage Gateway
Automatically archive old objects → Lifecycle policy
sections.callout: Identify the storage model and persistence requirement first.

entries.title: S3 vs. EBS
paragraphs: Object storage → S3. Persistent block volume for EC2 → EBS.

entries.title: EBS vs. Instance Store
paragraphs: Persistent block volume → EBS. Temporary host-attached storage → Instance store.

entries.title: EFS vs. EBS
paragraphs: Shared Linux file system → EFS. Block volume → EBS.

entries.title: EFS vs. FSx
paragraphs: Elastic shared Linux NFS → EFS. Specialized managed file-system technology → FSx.

entries.title: Lifecycle vs. Backup
paragraphs: Transition or expire objects as they age → Lifecycle. Create and manage backups → AWS Backup.
